requirements.quote: Enumeration HEX Meaning 0 0x00 Connection Accepted 1 0x01 Connection Refused: unacceptable protocol version 2 0x02 Connection Refused: identifier rejected 3 0x03 Connection Refused: broker unavailable 4-255 Reserved for future use
requirements.condition: When encoding or interpreting a connection return code.
requirements.required_behavior: Use 0/0x00 for Connection Accepted, 1/0x01 for unacceptable protocol version, 2/0x02 for identifier rejected, and 3/0x03 for broker unavailable.
requirements.why_checkable: The numeric return-code values and their meanings can be checked directly.

requirements.quote: Enumeration HEX Meaning 0 0x00 Connection Accepted 1 0x01 Connection Refused: unacceptable protocol version 2 0x02 Connection Refused: identifier rejected 3 0x03 Connection Refused: broker unavailable 4-255 Reserved for future use
requirements.condition: When selecting a connection return code.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use values 4 through 255 for defined current meanings; they are reserved for future use.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's emitted and accepted return-code values can be checked against the reserved range.

requirements.quote: The topic name is present in the variable header of an MQTT PUBLISH message.
requirements.condition: For an MQTT PUBLISH message.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the topic name in the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: A PUBLISH encoder or parser can be inspected to determine whether its variable header contains the topic name.

requirements.quote: The topic name is a UTF-encoded string.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a topic name.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the topic name as a UTF-encoded string.
requirements.why_checkable: The topic-name wire representation can be validated against the stated string encoding.

requirements.quote: Topic name has an upper length limit of 32,767 characters.
requirements.condition: For any topic name.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit the topic name to at most 32,767 characters.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept or generate a topic name longer than 32,767 characters.
requirements.why_checkable: Topic-name character length can be measured and compared with the fixed upper bound.

requirements.quote: The following types of MQTT command message have a payload: CONNECT The payload contains one or three UTF-8 encoded strings.
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT command message.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a payload containing exactly one or exactly three UTF-8 encoded strings.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a CONNECT payload with exactly two strings or more than three strings.
requirements.why_checkable: The number and encoding of strings in a CONNECT payload can be counted and validated.

requirements.quote: The first string uniquely identifies the client to the broker.
requirements.condition: For the first string in a CONNECT payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the first string as an identifier that uniquely identifies the client to the broker.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation can be tested for consistent unique client identification at the broker.

requirements.quote: The second string is the Will topic, and the third string is the Will message.
requirements.condition: When a CONNECT payload contains three strings.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Will topic as the second string and the Will message as the third string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reverse or otherwise reorder the Will topic and Will message.
requirements.why_checkable: The semantic role and order of the second and third payload strings can be inspected on the wire.

requirements.quote: The second and third strings are present only if the Will flag is set in the CONNECT Flags byte.
requirements.condition: When processing the Will flag and CONNECT payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the second and third strings to be present only when the Will flag is set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include the second or third string when the Will flag is clear.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag value can be correlated directly with presence or absence of the two Will strings.

requirements.quote: SUBSCRIBE The payload contains a list of topic names to which the client can subscribe, and the QoS level. These strings are UTF-encoded.
requirements.condition: For a SUBSCRIBE command message.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode its payload as a list of UTF-encoded topic names together with the QoS level.
requirements.why_checkable: A SUBSCRIBE payload can be parsed to verify the presence and encoding of topic names and associated QoS information.

requirements.quote: SUBACK The payload contains a list of granted QoS levels.
requirements.condition: For a SUBACK command message.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a payload containing a list of granted QoS levels.
requirements.why_checkable: The SUBACK payload structure can be parsed and checked for the QoS-level list.

requirements.quote: Granted QoS levels are listed in the same order as the topic names in the corresponding SUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.condition: When producing a SUBACK for a corresponding SUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.required_behavior: List granted QoS levels in the same order as the topic names in that SUBSCRIBE message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reorder granted QoS results relative to their corresponding SUBSCRIBE topic names.
requirements.why_checkable: A SUBSCRIBE topic sequence can be compared positionally with the resulting SUBACK QoS sequence.

requirements.quote: The payload part of a PUBLISH message contains application-specific data only.
requirements.condition: For the payload of a PUBLISH message.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the payload only for application-specific data.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place MQTT control-header fields in the PUBLISH payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoder's field placement and resulting wire message can be inspected.

requirements.quote: No assumptions are made about the nature or content of the data, and this part of the message is treated as a BLOB.
requirements.condition: When MQTT processes a PUBLISH payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the payload as an opaque BLOB without imposing assumptions about its nature or content.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not require an MQTT-level application-data format or interpretation.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can supply arbitrary byte content and verify that MQTT transports it opaquely.

requirements.quote: If you want an application to apply compression to the payload data, you need to define in the application the appropriate payload flag fields to handle the compression details.
requirements.condition: If an application applies compression to payload data.
requirements.required_behavior: Define the flags needed for compression details within the application payload scheme.
requirements.why_checkable: A compression-enabled application protocol can be inspected for its payload-level signaling fields.

requirements.quote: You cannot define application-specific flags in the fixed or variable headers.
requirements.condition: When defining application-specific signaling.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not define application-specific flags in MQTT fixed or variable headers.
requirements.why_checkable: Header layouts and application extensions can be inspected for application-specific flag bits.

requirements.quote: The message identifier is present in the variable header of the following MQTT messages: PUBLISH, PUBACK, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP, SUBSCRIBE, SUBACK, UNSUBSCRIBE, UNSUBACK. The Message Identifier (Message ID) field is only present in messages where the QoS bits in the fixed header indicate QoS levels 1 or 2.
requirements.condition: For a listed MQTT message whose fixed-header QoS bits indicate QoS level 1 or 2.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Message ID field in the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The message type and QoS bits can be correlated with Message ID presence in the variable header.

requirements.quote: The Message Identifier (Message ID) field is only present in messages where the QoS bits in the fixed header indicate QoS levels 1 or 2.
requirements.condition: When the fixed-header QoS bits do not indicate QoS level 1 or 2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include the Message ID field.
requirements.why_checkable: A parser or encoder can be tested for Message ID absence under other QoS values.

requirements.quote: The Message ID is a 16-bit unsigned integer.
requirements.condition: When encoding or storing a Message ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the Message ID as a 16-bit unsigned integer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode a Message ID outside the 16-bit unsigned representation.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and numeric range are directly measurable.

requirements.quote: It typically increases by exactly one from one message to the next, but is not required to do so.
requirements.condition: When assigning successive Message IDs.
requirements.why_checkable: The sentence explicitly says the typical increment is not required, so it supplies no mandatory implementation constraint.

requirements.quote: This assumes that there are never more than 65,535 messages "in flight" between one particular client-broker pair at any time.
requirements.condition: For messages in flight between one particular client-broker pair.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the number of simultaneously in-flight messages at or below 65,535.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not have more than 65,535 messages in flight between the same client-broker pair at one time.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's per-pair in-flight message count can be measured against the stated bound.

requirements.quote: The ordering of the two bytes of the Message Identifier is MSB, then LSB (big-endian).
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the two-byte Message Identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Order the bytes as MSB first and LSB second, using big-endian order.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode the Message Identifier in little-endian order.
requirements.why_checkable: The two wire bytes can be inspected for byte order.

requirements.quote: Do not use Message ID 0. It is reserved as an invalid Message ID.
requirements.condition: When assigning or validating a Message ID.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat Message ID 0 as invalid and reserved.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use Message ID 0.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated and accepted identifiers can be tested for rejection or non-use of zero.

requirements.quote: The MQTT protocol uses a subset of UTF-8. Only single byte (non-extended) characters are supported.
requirements.condition: When MQTT encodes or accepts a UTF-8 string.
requirements.required_behavior: Support only single-byte, non-extended characters.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode or accept multibyte extended UTF-8 characters.
requirements.why_checkable: String bytes can be inspected to distinguish single-byte characters from multibyte UTF-8 sequences.

requirements.quote: bit 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0 byte 1 Message Length MSB byte 2 Message Length LSB bytes 3 ... Encoded Character Data
requirements.condition: When encoding an MQTT UTF string.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the string with the message-length MSB in byte 1, the message-length LSB in byte 2, and encoded character data beginning at byte 3.
requirements.why_checkable: The prefix bytes and start position of character data can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote: Message Length is the number of bytes of encoded string characters, not the number of characters.
requirements.condition: When calculating the length prefix of an encoded string.
requirements.required_behavior: Set Message Length to the number of bytes of encoded string characters.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not calculate Message Length as the character count when that differs from the encoded-byte count.
requirements.why_checkable: The length prefix can be compared with the actual encoded-data byte count.

requirements.quote: The format of encoded characters for ASCII codes 0x01 to 0x7F are shown in the table below. bit 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0 0 ASCII code of character
requirements.condition: When encoding an ASCII character with code 0x01 through 0x7F.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode it as one byte whose high bit is 0 and whose remaining bits contain the ASCII character code.
requirements.why_checkable: Each encoded ASCII byte can be checked for the specified bit layout and code range.

requirements.quote: bit 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0 byte 1 Message Type (1) DUP flag QoS level RETAIN 0 0 0 1 x x x x byte 2 Remaining Length
requirements.condition: For the fixed header of a CONNECT message.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Message Type as 1 in the high nibble of byte 1 and encode Remaining Length beginning in byte 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT fixed-header bytes can be checked against the stated bit layout.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flags are not used in the CONNECT message.
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT message.
requirements.required_behavior: Do not assign DUP, QoS, or RETAIN semantics to its fixed-header low-nibble flags.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use the DUP, QoS, or RETAIN flags in CONNECT.
requirements.why_checkable: CONNECT encoding and processing can be inspected for use of these flags.

requirements.quote: Remaining Length is the length of the variable header (12 bytes) and the length of the Payload.
requirements.condition: When calculating Remaining Length for a CONNECT message.
requirements.required_behavior: Set Remaining Length to 12 bytes plus the length of the payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Remaining Length can be compared with the fixed 12-byte variable header plus measured payload length.

requirements.quote: This can be a multibyte field.
requirements.condition: When Remaining Length requires more than one byte.
requirements.required_behavior: Support a multibyte representation of Remaining Length.
requirements.why_checkable: CONNECT messages with sufficiently large payloads can verify multibyte Remaining Length handling.

requirements.quote: Protocol Name byte 1 Length MSB (0) 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 byte 2 Length LSB (6) 0 0 0 0 0 1 1 0 byte 3 'M' 0 1 0 0 1 1 0 1 byte 4 'Q' 0 1 0 1 0 0 0 1 byte 5 'I' 0 1 0 0 1 0 0 1 byte 6 's' 0 1 1 1 0 0 1 1 byte 7 'd' 0 1 1 0 0 1 0 0 byte 8 'p' 0 1 1 1 0 0 0 0 Protocol Version Number byte 9 Version (3) 0 0 0 0 0 0 1 1
requirements.condition: When encoding the CONNECT variable header.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the protocol name as a six-byte string "MQIsdp" preceded by length bytes 0 and 6, and encode protocol version 3 in byte 9.
requirements.why_checkable: Bytes 1 through 9 of the CONNECT variable header can be compared directly with the stated values.

requirements.quote: An example of the format of the variable header is shown in the table below.
requirements.condition: For the following CONNECT variable-header table.
requirements.why_checkable: The source labels the table as an example, leaving unclear which displayed flag and timer values are universal constraints.

requirements.quote: The payload of the CONNECT message contains one or three UTF-encoded strings.
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT message payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Contain exactly one or exactly three UTF-encoded strings.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not contain exactly two strings or more than three strings.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT payload can be parsed to count its UTF-encoded strings.

requirements.quote: If the Will flag is set in the Connect flags byte in the variable header, the payload must contain all three UTF-encoded strings:
requirements.condition: If the Will flag is set in the CONNECT flags byte.
requirements.required_behavior: Include all three UTF-encoded strings in the CONNECT payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send a one-string CONNECT payload while the Will flag is set.
requirements.why_checkable: The Will flag can be correlated with the exact count of strings in the CONNECT payload.

requirements.quote: Client Identifier The first UTF-encoded string.
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the Client Identifier as the first UTF-encoded string.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not place another CONNECT payload field before the Client Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The first payload field can be parsed and identified as the Client Identifier.

requirements.quote: The Client Identifier (Client ID) is between 1 and 23 characters long, and uniquely identifies the client to the broker.
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT Client Identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a Client Identifier whose length is from 1 through 23 characters inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use an empty Client Identifier or one longer than 23 characters.
requirements.why_checkable: The Client Identifier's character length can be measured against the inclusive bounds.

requirements.quote: The Client Identifier (Client ID) is between 1 and 23 characters long, and uniquely identifies the client to the broker.
requirements.condition: When a client connects to a broker.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a Client Identifier that uniquely identifies that client to the broker.
requirements.why_checkable: Concurrent or persisted broker client identities can be tested for uniqueness by Client ID.
